messages:
maya: quick FYI — spotted a prod sampled request where a base64 PDF in `doc_blob` contained email addresses and our redactor missed them. :grimacing:
ajit: ugh. do you have the trace/id? was this in sampled telemetry or in full audit logs?
maya: trace: https://console.redwood/prod/trace/0e7a — sampled telemetry only (sampled=1). payload snippet:```curl -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/generate -d '{\n  "prompt": "summarize invoice",\n  "doc_blob": "JVBERi0xLjQKJcfs...base64...QmVuZHN0cmVhbQ=="\n}'```
sam: looks like our redaction applies to `prompt` and `attachments[*].text` but we treat `doc_blob` as opaque string and only hash it for dedupe. so inner plaintext (emails) in decoded payload won't be scrubbed.
elaine: that explains the leak. two things: (1) adding `doc_blob` to fields_to_redact is easy but will cause tokenization/encoding overhead in the redactor, and (2) console metrics like `request_size` and token counts will change if we drop/strip blobs.
ajit: agree. proposal: detect base64 blobs heuristically, mark them as binary and redact whole blob (replace with `<<BINARY_REDACTED, mime=image/pdf, len=23456>>`) — avoid decoding/tokenizing at all.
jeff: +1 on binary marker. but we need a shim for telemetry: keep an integer field `attachment_bytes` and `attachment_count` so quotas and dashboards still reflect size without raw content.
sam: pseudo-config patch:```json
{
  "redactor": {
    "fields_to_redact": ["prompt", "attachments[*].text"],
    "blob_policy": {
      "detect_base64": true,
      "treat_as_binary": ["doc_blob","attachments[*].data"],
      "replacement_template": "<<BINARY_REDACTED, mime={mime}, len={bytes}>>"
    }
  }
}
```
elaine: console UX note — when we show inspect preview we currently allow temporary unmask if user has `inspect:unmask`. For binary blobs we should never allow unmasking (legal/safety). Also add a flag in the inspect UI that shows `attachment_bytes` and a download button only for enterprise with HSM audit.
maya: also: this was only in sampled logs but inspect mode might unmask sampled items for SREs. do we want to change inspect-ttl or require re-authorization?
ajit: let's tighten: sampled inspect entries require secondary auth and the `inspect_ttl` for sampled logs becomes 15m by default (instead of 24h). we can add an allowlist for legal/team.
ops-bot: deploybot: queued rollout redactor/v2 (binary-blobs) -> canary on staging at 2024-10-03T23:12Z — https://deploys.redwood/redactor/v2
jeff: telemetry: add `attachment_bytes` histogram and update quota plane to count that towards `ingress_bytes`. also update dashboard widget to sum `attachment_bytes` per route.
sam: action items: 1) PR to redactor to add base64 detection + replacement template (owner: sam) 2) console change to never unmask binary and surface attachment_bytes (owner: elaine) 3) quota/telemetry change to add attachment_bytes metric (owner: jeff) 4) tighten sampled inspect TTL + secondary auth (owner: ajit) — canary after staging pass.
maya: thanks all — i'm going to open the incident ticket and paste repro. :eyes:
ajit: cool. @sam plz link PR when ready, we can small-canary on a subset of tenants. :shipit:
jeff: noted, I'll add a dashboard drilldown so SREs can quickly filter routes with high `attachment_bytes`.
maya: marking resolved for now — followups in the ticket. :white_check_mark:
